title: Fish Without a Bicycle
full_review:
Jenna Mattison wrote, produced and stars in "Fish Without a Bicycle" (Newmark/Echelon), a mostly unappealing story about an L.A.-based actress -- Catholic, as it happens -- and her all-important quest to "find herself," as she dumps her fireman boyfriend for a self-absorbed director (Bryan Callen).

Meanwhile, she ignores the gentlemanly advances of her decent-guy acting partner (Brian A. Green, who also directed), seemingly the ideal mate for her. On top of all this, her sardonic best friend (Jennifer Blanc) suddenly reveals a lesbian attraction to her.
Occasional flashes of wit and some good supporting performances fail to balance the low-budget production values, gratuitously frank sex talk and implied activity that tries to outdo "Sex and the City." A leading lady with a fatal case of the cutes relegates the film squarely to the category of a sappy vanity production.

Because of much rough and profane language, sexual situations, vulgarity and a questionable worldview, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
